sources.title: eCFR — 42 CFR 483.15 (Admission, transfer, and discharge rights)
sources.source_date: the page carries its own 'up to date as of ...' and 'last amended ...' statement, not pinned to a capture date
sources.notes: Plain curl with no user-agent 302-redirects to unblock.federalregister.gov's bot-check page; a browser user-agent reaches the real server-rendered page (no __NEXT_DATA__ island) with a 200. div[id="483.15"] is the section's own container, confirmed to hold the whole section text and nothing of the neighboring sections 483.10/483.20. The eCFR versioner API (title-42 XML pinned to a point-in-time issue date) is the transport the standing packet's 2026-09-27 capture notes record, but that date goes stale every time the title is amended and the API has no 'latest' alias; fetching the site's own /current/ page instead gets the same text from the publisher's always-current rendering, with no date to maintain in the recipe.

sources.title: CMS State Operations Manual, Appendix PP (Guidance to Surveyors for Long Term Care Facilities), tags F622–F628
sources.notes: 926-page manual; plain curl with no user-agent returns 200 directly. -layout is used because the manual is single-column and -layout preserves the printed indentation (the lettered/numbered sub-paragraph hanging indents) that -raw would collapse. No page numbers or running headers survive extraction in this span, so neither of those filters is needed; join-wrap-hyphens rejoins the handful of column-width line-wraps inside compound words (post-acute, non-payment, person-centered) with the hyphen kept, matching the standing packet. The slice runs from F622's own revision line through to F636's, a superset: it holds all of F622-F628 plus F635, the same span the hand capture held, because the tags most readers would call relevant to transfer/discharge and bed-hold run together as one continuous block and a tidy stop at F628 would cut mid-topic.
